title: Choose the first safe HDFS recovery action
description: Inject a storage or control-plane failure, set a repair bandwidth ceiling, and see whether the selected response restores the broken invariant.

actions.label: Restore rack-aware replica count
actions.detail: Prioritize endangered blocks, add healthy targets, and verify placement diversity.

actions.label: Fence and fail over the NameNode
actions.detail: Prevent split brain, promote the synchronized standby, and verify namespace health.

actions.label: Quarantine corrupt replicas
actions.detail: Stop serving bad blocks, copy from verified replicas, and re-run checksum scans.

actions.label: Run the cluster balancer
actions.detail: Move healthy blocks to reduce long-lived disk-utilization skew.

scenarios.label: Two DataNodes fail
scenarios.detail: A shared power fault removes two dense nodes while the remaining cluster still serves reads.
scenarios.explanation: Prioritize blocks with the fewest surviving copies, restore rack-aware placement, and keep enough free disk and bandwidth for re-replication.

scenarios.label: Active NameNode disappears
scenarios.detail: Clients lose namespace operations even though DataNode block files remain intact.
scenarios.explanation: Fence the old active process before promoting the synchronized standby; the SecondaryNameNode is not a hot failover target.

scenarios.label: Checksum corruption spreads
scenarios.detail: Readers detect corrupt replicas for a hot dataset after a controller fault.
scenarios.explanation: Quarantine bad replicas, reconstruct from verified copies, and confirm checksums before returning blocks to service.

scenarios.label: New nodes remain empty
scenarios.detail: Capacity was added, but old DataNodes remain near their high-water marks and jobs avoid the new disks.
scenarios.explanation: Run a bounded balancer and watch rack traffic so healthy replicas move without disrupting foreground jobs.
